lessons.title: क्यों (kyoṁ) — why
lessons.gloss: why — the k- word the deixis lesson listed and never taught

segments.text: Retrieve the two items before this one by name: सकना and चाहना. Then run the k- words the deixis lesson gave you — क्या, कहाँ, and kaun. There is one more in that family, and it is the one a listener most often wants.
आप क्यों नहीं आ सकते? — āp kyoṁ nahīṁ ā sakte? — Why can't you come?

क्यों (kyoṁ) goes where any Hindi question word goes: in the sentence's ordinary slot, in front of the verb — not dragged to the front the way English drags why. The rest of the sentence keeps the order it always had, verb last.
On its own, क्यों (kyoṁ)? is a complete turn. It is how you ask somebody to explain what they have just said, and it costs one syllable.

The deixis lesson generalised the य- / व- / क- system and listed the k- words. This is one of the ones it listed and did not teach. Its क- is the same ancient stem as क्या and kaun, and it is Latin's qu- in quis and English's wh- in who — one Indo-European kʷ-, three different spellings of the same sound.

segments.instruction: kyoṁ? on its own, as a whole turn
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *kyoṁ?* on its own, as a whole turn]

segments.instruction: the four k- words together — kyā, kaun, kahāṁ, kyoṁ
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the four k- words together — *kyā*, *kaun*, *kahāṁ*, *kyoṁ*]

segments.prompt: Ask why the listener cannot come.

feedback.correct: The question word stays in the sentence's own slot.
feedback.incorrect: Leave the word order alone and put kyoṁ in front of the verb.

segments.text: Where does क्यों (kyoṁ) stand in the sentence? (In its ordinary slot, in front of the verb — not fronted.) Which family does it belong to? (The k- question words.)

lessons.title: क्योंकि (kyoṁki) — because
lessons.gloss: because — literally why-that, the question word and the complementiser welded into one

segments.text: Ask क्यों (kyoṁ)? out loud. Then notice that you have no way at all to answer it. Now say कि — the word from the last chapter that hangs a clause on a verb. The answer is those two words stuck together.
मैं कल नहीं आ सकता क्योंकि मैं काम करता हूँ. — maiṁ kal nahīṁ ā saktā kyoṁki maiṁ kām kartā hūṁ. — I can't come tomorrow because I work.
Read the word: क्योंकि (kyoṁki) is क्यों + कि, why-that. Nothing is hidden in it. Hindi answers why by saying why-that and then a whole ordinary sentence, verb last, exactly as after plain कि.
The order is fixed and it is the useful way round: the claim first, the reason second. English can lead with because; the ordinary Hindi sentence does not.

That example is worth memorising whole, because it is the shape of an entire exam task: a written message that says you cannot meet and why. It needs three things this book has now given you — the negation, सकना, and क्योंकि (kyoṁki) — and it needed all three.

Look at what the word is made of one more time. क्यों (kyoṁ) comes down from Sanskrit; कि was borrowed from Persian. Hindi welded them into a single conjunction and nobody notices the seam. That is this language in one word.

segments.text: What two words is क्योंकि (kyoṁki) made of? (क्यों + कि.) Which half of a क्योंकि (kyoṁki) sentence comes first? (The claim; the reason follows.)

lessons.title: Two turns: why, and because
lessons.gloss: asking for a reason and giving one, in two turns

segments.text: क्योंकि (kyoṁki) is two words you already had. Say them apart, then together, then say where the verb of each half sits.
Reach back three chapters while you are here: या offers a choice and लेकिन contradicts. Neither can give a reason, which is what this chapter added.

segments.prompt: Take both turns: ask why the listener cannot come, then answer with a reason.
acceptedResponses: āp kyoṁ nahīṁ ā sakte? — maiṁ kal nahīṁ ā saktā kyoṁki maiṁ kām kartā hūṁ
आप क्यों नहीं आ सकते? मैं कल नहीं आ सकता क्योंकि मैं काम करता हूँ

feedback.correct: A question and a reason: the smallest complete exchange in the book.
feedback.incorrect: Ask with kyoṁ, answer with the claim first and kyoṁki before the reason.

segments.text: Which word asks for a reason, and which gives one? (क्यों asks, क्योंकि (kyoṁki) gives.) What is the second one made of? (The first one, plus कि.) Then stop.
